title: When a State Slides Back / 国家怎样往回滑？
scope: Three companion reader essays from the new State Theory special study, in complete Simplified and Traditional Chinese and independently written English. Original eight-essay numbering and article texts retained; no new ep08 is invented.
method: Lead read the full 44,801-character Chinese source including the collected propositions, references and handoffs. Three explicitly authorized subagents drafted one Chinese essay and independent English rewrite each; lead read both languages and all three generated Traditional Chinese bodies, unified institution names, added explicit oversight/enforcement distinctions, edited prose, and verified source boundaries and integration. Sites skill used for local-only existing-repository implementation and local preview; no hosted Site creation or deployment.

source.verification: Fresh HTTPS fetch matched the author’s local paper byte for byte, 2026-10-29. Source paper not edited.

coverage.focus: Genuine threat within a fictional case versus added powers; four non-inevitable movements; formal legality versus effective questioning; independent judicial judgment versus threshold and enforcement; evidence limits; affected minorities; directions not permanent state identities.

Original fictional route stops before consolidation. A remaining unused amendment route is distinct from the actual decisions that reopen elections; external conditions and internal procedures jointly matter. Blocking a new step differs from restoring prior safeguards. Repair, independent appointment review, continuing judgment validity, non-erased accountability and the next window’s inherited tools.

Explicit counterfactual alternative, not the canonical ending; proposed five-route closure assessment; prospective evidence only; differentiated bilateral cooperation after recognizing consolidation versus act-specific responses before it; recognition, cooperation and accountability; humanitarian paths; responding state’s own acts remain reviewable.

Brief contextual dialogue with Plato and Montesquieu, checked against primary texts. Difference of focus from constitutional decline, rulers’ psychology and animating principles, not an assertion that either philosopher is refuted.

primary_references.scope: Republic, Book VIII: constitutional changes and dispositions; governing division; protector and tyranny. No direct quotation used in the companion landing page.

Janet edition appendix: Book VIII chapters I and XI; corruption of animating principles and effects on laws. Main edition title covers I–V; the cited VIII occurs in the appendix. No direct quotation used.

boundaries: All countries, years, votes and wartime events are the source’s fictional case, not a coded diagnosis of actual states or an empirical historical proof. Normative requirements are not claims about current law or prescriptions for an actual diplomatic response.

The original UCSE route stops; the alternative changes events only from Year 10 winter through Year 12. Events in that branch cannot become original-case facts, and spring decisions cannot borrow evidence from summer.

A wrong act is not a permanent identity or sufficient proof of a systemic slide; multiple closures affecting a minority count even when majority institutions remain. Four movements are not an inevitable sequence or prediction.

Appointment, party affiliation, report counts and temporal proximity are not alone proof of capture or retaliation. A valid independent judgment may be blocked at execution without becoming invalid or proving the court controlled.

Philosophical limits, suggested revisable rules and officeholders’ concrete judgments remain distinct. The proposed five-channel assessment is the author’s rule proposal, not a universal legal test; merely unfair access is not complete closure under it. Vetoing a further step is not necessarily reopening closed routes; exit is separate.

Absence of a superior is the condition preventing correction from above, not an automatic causal explanation or destiny. Surviving channels do not guarantee reversal; external ceasefire and withdrawal conditions are not themselves institutional channels.

Return does not authorize the returning executive to decide contested judicial appointments or erase all rulings; role-specific independent assessment is distinguished from collective purge. Historical accountability need not mean mandatory prosecution; reform and restored cooperation do not erase the record.

System-level distancing is tied to independently recognizing consolidation. Before that threshold the source still permits questioning, records and necessary cooperation withdrawal targeted to particular acts; this is not a demand to wait silently.

Recognition here identifies the source position and attribution of acts, not moral endorsement or recognition of a state as a human subject. Outsiders adjust their own cooperation, not install another government or impose an ideological destination.

Cooperation withdrawal itself is reviewable; civilian life, actual access to protection and challenge, and non-nationality-based treatment are not discarded. Missing treaty provisions and effects are not filled in. Decline alone is not grounds for war; no actual legal compliance or political outcome is presumed.
